title: Dark Matter as Cosmic Scaffold: Galaxy Formation and Dark Matter-Deficient Systems
abstract: Dark matter constitutes 84% of cosmic matter and provides the gravitational scaffolding for galaxy formation. Without it, CMB fluctuations at small scales would be erased for baryonic matter. Dark matter-deficient galaxies (e.g., NGC 1052 DF2) challenge standard models but can be explained by tidal stripping, tidal formation, or high-speed collisions. These systems constrain dissipative and ultralight fuzzy dark matter models.

c9_implications.structure_formation: Dark matter halo merger trees are the backbone of cosmic assembly index (A_c) computation.
c9_implications.dark_sector: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) would modify halo profiles and affect A_c at galactic scales.
c9_implications.constraints: DF2-like systems rule out dissipative DM (would clump) and ultralight fuzzy DM (would escape shallow potentials).
